research_rationale:
Identity: the held registered text of Executive Order 14052 is the official Federal Register text layer at 86 FR 64335, PDF pages 1-2 (Federal Register / Vol. 86, No. 220 / Thursday, November 18, 2021); it names Executive Order 14052 of November 15, 2021, Implementation of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, and runs from the title to the signature block. The complete clause inventory was checked against the numbered section headings of that text. Section 2(pp) of Executive Order 14148 of January 20, 2025 (Initial Rescissions of Harmful Executive Orders and Actions, 90 FR 8237, Federal Register of January 28, 2025) lists Executive Order 14052 of November 15, 2021 among the executive actions that section 2 declares hereby revoked. The held text of Executive Order 14148 states no effective date later than its signing, so the revocation operates from its signing date, 2025-01-20. Whole-order revocation by name is the first end of every clause that had not already been exhausted by performance. The order has no other ending instrument before 2025-01-20 in the packet's later-event chain, which for this order lists besides Executive Order 14148: Executive Order 14082. The only other instrument in that chain, Executive Order 14082 of 2022-09-12, amends section 3(d) of this order; it is recorded as a later event on the affected clauses and is an amendment, not an end. The packet's name search of held order texts for this order's number returned no held text dated after Executive Order 14148 other than that order itself. The later-source search is recorded by the three machine searches selected on the sheet: the U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09), the eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with the CFR bulk files, and the Federal Register executive-order disposition catalog; their coverage statements were read and each is marked complete. Savings are addressed in the savings statement. The first end of the whole order is 2025-01-20.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Checked whether any clause ended before 2025-01-20. The held own text of Executive Order 14052 contains no provision that terminates or sets an expiry date for the order or for any clause; deadlines in clauses are performance dates, not ends. No earlier revocation, supersession or amendment that ends a clause is shown in the packet's later-event chain; the instruments it lists other than Executive Order 14148 are addressed in the clause reasons and source notes.","independent_command_check":"Every clause recorded for Executive Order 14052 is a statement or command of that order itself. Statutes, regulations and other instruments that the order cites keep whatever force they have independently of it, but they are not clauses of the order, so no independent command keeps any clause running after the revocation.","savings_check":"Savings were examined in the order's own text and in Executive Order 14148: section 2 contains no saving clause for the revoked orders, section 3(b) leaves existing actions to later review, and section 4 saves only statutory authority and Office of Management and Budget functions. The state is transferred_or_accrued for actions already taken, with no specific surviving action identified from held sources.","scope_check":"Section 2 of Executive Order 14148 revokes the order as a whole by number and by title, without limiting words and without excepting any clause, so the ending is not confined to part of the order. Section 4(a) of Executive Order 14148 states that nothing in it impairs the authority granted by law to an agency or the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget; that preserves statutory authority and does not preserve any clause of this order."}

savings.reason: Section 3(b) of Executive Order 14148 directs the Director of the Domestic Policy Council and the Director of the National Economic Council to review all Federal Government actions taken pursuant to the orders, memoranda and proclamations listed in section 2 and to take necessary steps to rescind, replace or amend such actions as appropriate. Because rescission of actions already taken is left to later action, Federal actions already taken under Executive Order 14052 before 2025-01-20 were not themselves revoked by section 2 and stood until rescinded, replaced or amended individually. No held source identifies a particular surviving action or its later fate, so none is asserted.
